thinkers.name: Philo of Alexandria (c. 20 BCE–50 CE)
thinkers.contribution: Pioneered allegorical interpretation of the Pentateuch; formulated the concept of the Logos as the divine mind and creative instrument of God.

thinkers.name: Saadia Gaon (882–942 CE)
thinkers.contribution: Demonstrated that divine revelation and human reason (aql) are mutually harmonious; categorized commandments into rational laws (mitzvot sikhliyyot) and revelatory laws (mitzvot shim'iyyot).

thinkers.name: Moses Maimonides (Rambam, 1138–1204 CE)
thinkers.contribution: Radical negative theology (Via Negativa: God can only be described by what He is not); uncompromising rejection of anthropomorphism; formulated the Thirteen Principles of Faith (Shloshah Asar Ikkarim).

thinkers.name: Hasdai Crescas (c. 1340–1410 CE)
thinkers.contribution: Rigorous critique of Aristotelian physics and Maimonidean rationalism; emphasized divine love, joy, and emotional devotion over pure intellect.

thinkers.name: Baruch Spinoza (1632–1677 CE)
thinkers.contribution: Excommunicated by Amsterdam Portuguese-Jewish community; pioneered modern historical-critical biblical criticism; formulated pantheism/panentheism (Deus sive Natura).

thinkers.name: Moses Mendelssohn (1729–1786 CE)
thinkers.work: Jerusalem: Or on Religious Power and Judaism (1783)
thinkers.contribution: Argued Judaism contains no dogmatic coercion of belief; Judaism is 'revealed legislation' rather than 'revealed dogma'; defended state religious toleration and separation of church and state.

thinkers.name: Martin Buber (1878–1965 CE)
thinkers.contribution: Distinguished between instrumental objectifying relationships (I-It) and genuine reciprocal encounters (I-Thou); God is the Eternal Thou met in relation with humanity and creation.

thinkers.name: Franz Rosenzweig (1886–1929 CE)
thinkers.work: Der Stern der Erlösung (The Star of Redemption, 1921)
thinkers.contribution: Formulated the relational triad of God, Man, and World linked by Creation, Revelation, and Redemption; viewed Judaism as eternal life within the covenant, while Christianity serves as eternal ray spreading outward to Gentiles.
